name: Fludrocortisone
originator: E. R. Squibb & Sons (Josef Fried and Emily Sabo)

discovery.by: Josef Fried and Emily Sabo, Squibb
discovery.note: Discovered that adding a fluorine at 9α of hydrocortisone hugely increases corticosteroid potency — the first fluorinated drug of its kind.

tagline: A potent salt-retaining steroid that replaces aldosterone
summary: Fludrocortisone is a synthetic corticosteroid with very strong mineralocorticoid activity, used to replace aldosterone in Addison's disease and salt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia. It is also used off-label to raise blood pressure in orthostatic hypotension.
mechanism: Fludrocortisone binds the mineralocorticoid receptor in the distal nephron and collecting duct, increasing expression of epithelial sodium channels and Na+/K+-ATPase. This increases sodium and water reabsorption and potassium and hydrogen-ion excretion, expanding plasma volume and raising blood pressure.
Its mineralocorticoid potency is about 125 times that of hydrocortisone, while glucocorticoid potency is about 10 times, so the low replacement doses have little glucocorticoid effect.
uses: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease), with a glucocorticoid

history.title: Addison's disease described
history.detail: Thomas Addison describes the clinical syndrome of adrenal insufficiency.

history.title: Aldosterone isolated
history.detail: Sylvia Simpson and James Tait isolate aldosterone, the natural mineralocorticoid.

history.title: Fluorine effect discovered
history.detail: Fried and Sabo report that 9α-fluorination of hydrocortisone greatly increases potency.

history.title: APROCCHSS trial
history.detail: Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone reduces 90-day mortality in septic shock compared with placebo (NEJM 2018).

facts: Fried and Sabo's 1954 discovery launched the era of fluorinated corticosteroids such as dexamethasone and betamethasone.
